title: Accenture style · Cognitive, Technical + Coding
description: Cognitive and technical MCQs followed by two coding problems. 90 MCQs + 2 coding problems in 135 minutes. Original practice questions modelled on the publicly reported test pattern. Not an official or past paper.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Good sleep is essential for learning. While we sleep, the brain sorts and stores what we learned during the day. Students who stay up all night before an exam often remember less than those who sleep well, even if they studied for more hours. Regular sleep times, less screen use before bed and a dark, quiet room all improve sleep quality.

Students who stay up all night before an exam
questions.explanation: The passage supports: often remember less.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The thief tried to ____ the police.
questions.explanation: Correct: The thief tried to elude the police.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) He (B) insisted to go (C) there (D) alone.
questions.explanation: ‘Insisted on going’.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘OBSOLETE’.
questions.explanation: ‘obsolete’ means outdated.

questions.text: What does the idiom ‘once in a blue moon’ mean?
questions.explanation: ‘once in a blue moon’ means: very rarely.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

India's digital payment system has grown remarkably. UPI allows instant transfers between bank accounts using a phone, and small shopkeepers now accept payments through QR codes. This has reduced the use of cash and made it easier to track transactions. Yet challenges remain: older people and those without smartphones can be left out, and online frauds have increased.

The word ‘remarkably’ is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The passage supports: strikingly.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The meeting was called ____ because of the storm.
questions.explanation: Correct: The meeting was called off because of the storm.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) Hardly had (B) I reached the station (C) than the train (D) left.
questions.explanation: ‘Hardly … when’.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘ADVERSITY’.
questions.explanation: ‘adversity’ means hardship.

questions.text: What does the idiom ‘throw in the towel’ mean?
questions.explanation: ‘throw in the towel’ means: give up.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Remote work was once rare in Indian companies. The pandemic forced firms to try it at scale, and many found that productivity did not fall. Employees saved hours of commuting, and companies saved on office space. However, new problems appeared: junior staff missed informal learning from seniors, and some people found it hard to separate work from home life. Many firms have now settled on a hybrid model, with two or three office days a week.

What made companies try remote work at scale?
questions.explanation: The passage supports: The pandemic.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The project was completed ____ time.
questions.explanation: Correct: The project was completed on time.

questions.explanation: Double comparative: ‘cleverer’.

questions.text:
Statements: Some cats are pens. All pens are doctors.
Conclusion: All cats are doctors.
Does the conclusion follow?
questions.explanation: Draw the Venn diagram for the statements: the conclusion fails in at least one possible case.

questions.text: In a certain code, TICKET is written as SHBJDS. How is PENCIL written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted -1 place in the alphabet.

questions.text: In a certain code, FLOWER is written as DJMUCP. How is SILVER written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted -2 places in the alphabet.

questions.text: In a survey, 26 people read newspaper A, 44 read B, 11 read both and 13 read neither. How many people read only one newspaper?
questions.explanation: Only A = 15, only B = 33; total = 48.

questions.text: In a row of 31 students, Chitra is 21st from the left. Gita is 9 places to the right of Chitra. What is Gita's position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Gita is 30th from the left, so 31 − 30 + 1 = 2nd from the right.

questions.text: A cube painted on all faces is cut into 125 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly three faces painted?
questions.explanation: For an n×n×n cube (n = 5): 3 faces: 8, 2 faces: 12(n−2), 1 face: 6(n−2)², none: (n−2)³ → 8.

questions.text: What comes next: GT, KP, OL, SH, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4; second letters move −4 from the other end of the alphabet.

questions.text: Which number is the odd one out: 344, 729, 8, 343?
questions.explanation: 344 — all others are perfect cubes.

questions.text: Pooja is taller than Nikhil. Nikhil is taller than Chitra. Chitra is taller than Zoya. Varun is taller than Pooja. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation: Chaining the clues: Varun > Pooja > Nikhil > Chitra > Zoya. The second tallest is Pooja.

questions.text: Meera is taller than Sneha. Varun is taller than Meera. Harsh is taller than Yash. Yash is taller than Varun. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation: Chaining the clues: Harsh > Yash > Varun > Meera > Sneha. The tallest is Harsh.

questions.text: Which number is the odd one out: 36, 66, 63, 117?
questions.explanation: 66 — all others are multiples of 9.

questions.text: Pooja is the mother of Uma. Varun is the son of Uma. How is Pooja related to Varun?
questions.explanation: Pooja is the mother of Varun's parent.

questions.text: In a row of 12 students, Yash is 5th from the left. Sneha is 2 places to the right of Yash. What is Sneha's position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Sneha is 7th from the left, so 12 − 7 + 1 = 6th from the right.

questions.text: Uma walks 8 m towards the East, then turns right and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 2 m, then turns right and walks 2 m. How far is Uma from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net displacement: 6 m east and 8 m south; distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
The rule is n → n² + n; for 10 it gives 110.

questions.text: In a certain code, MARKET is written as LZQJDS. How is PARROT written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted -1 place in the alphabet.

questions.text: Which number is the odd one out: 104, 107, 48, 64?
questions.explanation: 107 — all others are multiples of 8.

questions.text: Pointing to a man, Meera says, "His mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Meera related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Meera's mother is Meera herself, so Meera is his mother.
a ⊕ b = a² + b²; so 2 ⊕ 6 = 40.

questions.text: Jatin is the husband of Bharat. Farhan is the only grandchild of Rahul, who is Jatin's father. Farhan is the daughter of Bharat. How is Rahul related to Bharat?
questions.explanation: Rahul is the father of Bharat's husband.

questions.text: What is the sum of the first 16 terms of the series 9, 15, 21, ...?
Rs 7200 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 3 : 5 : 8. What is A's share?
A starts a business with Rs 7000. After 2 months B joins with Rs 10000. At the end of the year the profit is Rs 9200. What is B's share?
A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. In how many more days will A finish the job?
questions.explanation: In 2 days they do 1/3 of the work; 2/3 is left, which A does in 2/3 × 10 = 20/3 days.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 200 m and 250 m run at 72 km/h and 18 km/h in opposite directions. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s; distance = 450 m; time = 18 s.

questions.text: A starts a business with Rs 6000. After 2 months B joins with Rs 7000. At the end of the year the profit is Rs 14200. What is B's share?
The average age of 12 students is 59 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average increases by 2 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: New total = 61 × 13 = 793; old total = 708; teacher = 85.

questions.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 24 and 15 hours. Pipe C can empty it in 40 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/24 + 1/15 − 1/40 = 1/12 tank/hour, so 12 hours.

Read a word of lowercase letters and print each distinct letter with its count, in alphabetical order, one per line as ‘letter count’.

Input: one word (1 to 10^5 lowercase letters).
Output: one line per distinct letter.

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
